# Best power banks for charging a MacBook Pro

**Top pick: EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K (300W)**
- It has a built-in USB-C cable and two 140W ports, which is enough to fast-charge even a 16-inch MacBook Pro.
- Its 99.54Wh battery is just under the 100Wh airline carry-on limit.
- It weighs 24.7 oz (699g).
- Macworld lists it at $219.99 when reviewed, with one retailer at $109.99. WIRED shows $190 (down from $250), so prices vary a lot and are worth checking.
- [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/2955100/ecoflow-rapid-pro-27k-power-bank-300w-review-macbook-battery-pack.html) | [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-laptop-power-banks/)

**Other strong options**
- **Anker Prime 26K (300W):** Macworld's best overall pick. It has 140W PD 3.1 output, 250W input, and an app, but no built-in cable. [Macworld roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html)
- **INIU Cougar P64 (140W):** Macworld's value pick for 140W charging, though total output is low and there's no built-in cable. [Macworld roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html)
- **Sharge HyperTower 170 (100W):** Macworld's value pick at 100W, with two integrated cables. [Macworld roundup](https://www.macworld.com/article/2395511/best-laptop-power-banks-for-apple-macbook.html)
- **Anker Laptop Power Bank 25K (90Wh):** Engadget's best overall. In its test it gave a MacBook Pro about 0.68 of a full charge. [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/computing/accessories/best-laptop-power-bank-120040388.html)
- **Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100W):** about 74Wh, so it's carry-on legal, and $89.99 at Baseus's US store. It's fine for a 14-inch Pro, but a 16-inch under heavy load can draw more than 100W. Baseus doesn't publish how power splits across ports. [Buy via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)

**Caveats**
- The Dealectric page calls the Blade H1 "the only bank" with enough output for a MacBook Pro. That's wrong, since the Macworld, WIRED and Engadget guides list many 100W–140W options. Dealectric also earns a commission on its links.
- I only have review-page links from my search, not direct retailer links, so check current prices at the retailer of your choice.
- For a 16-inch Pro, choose a bank with at least one 140W port. For a 14-inch Pro or MacBook Air, 100W is enough.
- Stay under 100Wh if you plan to fly.

If you tell me which MacBook Pro you have and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
